title: Odds stacked against him: Shot at world record for waffle pile comes up short - NewsBreak
text:
By Kevin Lynch ,
19 hours ago
@good.morning.foodies Episode 71 - 08/04/2025 Can dice be Chaotic Evil?? Inspired by @Adventures In Aardia. #goodmorningfoodies #rollforbreakfast #dice #tasty #stayhungry ♬ original sound - Good Morning Foodies
A Millersburg man's attempt at getting into Guinness World Records came up short as his pile of waffles came crashing down.
Zach Didinger, a branch manager for Commercial & Savings Bank, who also hosts a breakfast TikTok channel, Good Morning Foodies , mixed his passion for breakfast and his competitive nature to pursue the world record for stacked waffles, which is 91.5 centimeters (a little more than three feet).
Didinger said he always has been fascinated by Guinness World Records and tried to think of something he could do to get his name in the book.
"I have always thought it would be so awesome to have a world record," he said. "Ever since I was in middle school, I was fascinated with the idea of having a world record.
"After doing quite a bit of research on different breakfast-themed Guinness World Records, I landed on the tallest stack of waffles," Didinger said. "This record seems difficult, but achievable."
A fun way to achieve a world record On Sunday, Aug. 24, at H15 Ministries in Millersburg, Didinger, with some help from his friends made the attempt.
"We made it to about 20 inches before the weight of the tower compressed the waffles underneath," Didinger said. "We made about 60 waffles, and each waffle was about an inch thick. We had the amount of waffles we needed, but as we got stacked up, we got to just shy of 20 inches, but the tower couldn't stand any more weight.
"We unstacked and stacked and rotated, but nothing we did seemed to help the compression," he said. "One of our viewers suggested the next time we try using gluten free dough, which makes the waffles a little more crispy."
It was a fun attempt at something he's always wanted to do, and he looks to possibly trying again.
"We did have a lot of fun and we have a lot of ideas if we decide to try it again in the future," Didinger added.
Crazy breakfast ideas led to Tik Tok channel
"I started filming and posting videos on TikTok this past February, and it kind of took off," he said. "My channel is all about breakfast, specifically wild and crazy breakfasts. I roll different dice to determine what ingredients I use to create my breakfast for the day."
This has created some crazy combinations, like French toast with taco sauce and ice cream and biscuits with blackberry jam and bacon or waffles with smoked salmon and peanut butter.
"Let's just say some breakfasts have turned out much better than others, but every video has been very fun to make," he said.
Requirements for the challenge Guinness requires the attempt at records to be held in a public location, and Didinger volunteers at H15 with the high school students, so it met the requirements.
"H15 is just an awesome place to come and hang out, filled with relational ministry," he said. "Having the record attempt here just made sense to me. Everyone could come here and enjoy the facility and then have a waffle, or two, or five or even 10. I do really enjoy waffles, but thankfully I do not have to eat this entire stack."
Another Guinness requirement was that all of the food has to be eaten, as they do not allow food to go to waste.
"We had plenty of helpers here and any of the remaining waffles were sent off to New Point Church for a youth event," he added.
